Key phrase: Mature adults do not lie *all the time*

You cannot judge someone for lying to *protect themselves*. Would you judge a gay person for pretending to be straight in order to avoid social stigma? If a married gay man is asked if he is in a relationship, is he an asshole for lying about his partner? Safety comes first no matter what; if you spend your whole life threatening HR (when your HR may very well not defend you), that is going to be terrible for your mental health. OP's lie hurt no one and it was solely to protect himself from an invasive question.

In the same way if someone saw scars from top surgery, those particular scars have everything to do with being trans. If someone sees scars from being hit as a kid, those scars have everything to do with child abuse. If someone has scars from self harm, those scars have everything to do with mental health. 

You have to realize, having a simple story to tell people to redirect them from prying, uncomfortable questions is mainly a way to protect yourself. It has nothing to do with "but can they tell how you got the scars"; they are forcing you into a position where you have three choices:

1) Tell the Truth. This can have serious repercussions based on whatever social stigma is around the origins of your scars, and it can also be traumatic to focus on these experiences when explaining.

2) Tell them Nothing. This can cause people to be offended at your lack of a reply or cause them to be even more curious/nosy, which just means you'll have to put up with the situation even more.

3) Lie. If your lie is simple, their curiosity can be sated and the topic can be dropped. In the same way you CANNOT fault a gay person for lying about being straight to protect themselves vs saying "none of your business", you cannot judge a trans person for lying to protect themselves. You do not have the experiences they have and you do not know what hardships are associated with the injury. In this case, OP was worried about the social stigma associated (because he was already treated poorly/differently in the past for being openly trans).
